headline: KSE-100 falls for a third straight session to 168,155 as political uncertainty and a China-driven oil-price surge outweigh Wall Street's rally to a Nasdaq record on cooling Fed-hike bets
mood: Locally risk-off, globally risk-on · oil and politics the swing factors

snapshot.label: Brent / WTI
snapshot.delta: China export halt · OPEC+ holds Nov output

five_things.html: The KSE-100 fell for a third straight session on Friday, settling at 168,155.49, down 481.36 points (−0.29%), after shedding 1,332.47 points (−0.78%) on Thursday — a combined roughly 1,814-point, 1.07% slide over two sessions — as local political uncertainty collided with a fresh oil-price surge. Total market volume slipped to 493.96 million shares (from 548.38 million) on traded value of Rs17.49 billion, with decliners leading advancers 321 to 128 (45 unchanged) across 494 names; Commercial Banks dragged the index down 121.77 points while Oil & Gas Exploration Companies added 72.68 points. The index opened Monday under renewed pressure, falling over 1,600 points intraday to 166,554.66 (−0.95%) as the same twin drivers persisted. Business Recorder and Mettis Global confirm the levels.
five_things.sentiment: three-day slide extends into Monday's open

five_things.chip: Wall Street Rallies as Jobs Miss Cools the Fed
five_things.html: US equities surged Friday after September payrolls rose just 29,000 (vs. 84,000 expected) and unemployment ticked up to 4.2%, cementing bets that the Fed holds at its 27–28 October meeting: the S&P 500 gained 0.73% to 7,722.72, the Dow added 0.49% (+250.40 pts) to 51,176.96, and the Nasdaq jumped 1.19% to a record-high 27,190.86. CME FedWatch priced October hike odds at roughly 17–21%, down from 64% a week earlier, even as Fed Vice Chair Jefferson and New York Fed's Williams counselled patience after Chair Warsh's hawkish September debut hike to 3.75–4%. Yahoo Finance and CNBC confirm the levels.
five_things.sentiment: soft jobs data, firmer risk appetite

five_things.chip: Yields Hold Near Highs as Oil Climbs, OPEC+ Steadies Supply
five_things.html: The 10-year Treasury yield closed at 5.28% and the 2-year at 4.83% — ticking higher even as the weak jobs print cooled October hike bets, underscoring a still-hawkish rate backdrop. Brent settled at $102.25 and WTI at $91.11, up roughly 2% on the week after China suspended oil-product exports and tightened global fuel supply, compounding lingering Strait of Hormuz disruption. OPEC+'s seven core producers agreed on 4 October to hold November output at 31.01 million bpd — extending October's pause after four straight monthly hikes — with Gulf members still pumping 60–80% of normal levels amid the Hormuz-linked export disruption. CNBC and CNBC confirm the levels.
five_things.sentiment: yields sticky, oil firm and supply-constrained

five_things.chip: Gold, Silver Give Back the Payrolls Bounce
five_things.html: Bullion's early jobs-data rally faded into the close: spot gold settled near $4,142.00, down 0.83% on the session, and spot silver fell 1.04% to $60.23, as a firm dollar and still-elevated Treasury yields outweighed the softer October rate-hike odds. Kitco and Fortune confirm the levels.

five_things.chip: SBP Holds at 11.5%, CPI Eases to 10.3%, IMF Review Advances
five_things.html: Pakistan's SBP held its policy rate at 11.5% for a third straight meeting on 14 September, as September CPI eased to 10.3% y/y (from August's 11.1%) — still well above the 5–7% target band, with transport costs up 27.4% y/y. The rupee firmed 3 paisa to 277.07 interbank, while 3-month KIBOR held near 11.78% and 6-month near 11.98% (as of 25 September). An IMF mission under Iva Petrova continues the fourth EFF/third RSF review, kicked off by Finance Minister Aurangzeb on 29 September; a successful conclusion would unlock roughly $1.2 billion combined, with Islamabad also requiring 10,000 federal employees to digitally declare assets by 30 October. Profit and Business Recorder confirm the details.

matrix.local_html: Pakistan's tape turned decisively risk-off into the weekend: the KSE-100 fell for a third straight session, down 481 points (−0.29%) Friday to 168,155.49 after shedding 1,332 points Thursday, as local political uncertainty collided with a fresh oil-price surge from China's export suspension. Commercial Banks led the damage (−121.77 index points) while Oil & Gas Exploration Companies cushioned the fall (+72.68 points) on firmer crude. The SBP held its policy rate at 11.5% on 14 September as September CPI eased to 10.3% y/y, and the rupee firmed marginally to 277.07 interbank even as the index opened Monday down a further 1,600-plus points to 166,554.66. The IMF's fourth EFF/third RSF review remains the key swing factor, with roughly $1.2bn in disbursements hinging on its outcome. Business Recorder and The Express Tribune.
matrix.gcc_html: Gulf fundamentals stayed anchored by non-oil momentum even as oil-market mechanics tightened. Saudi Arabia's Riyad Bank PMI held at a six-month high of 57.8 in September, as the Crown Prince's PIF 2026–2030 strategy cut construction spending by roughly $41 billion while elevating Hormuz-immune digital infrastructure as Vision 2030's new centre of gravity; non-oil activity now accounts for 55% of non-oil GDP. OPEC+'s seven core producers held November output at 31.01 million bpd on 4 October — extending the pause after four consecutive monthly hikes — with Gulf members still pumping only 60–80% of normal levels amid continuing Strait of Hormuz export disruption; the group next meets 1 November. Arab News and CNBC.
matrix.global_html: Wall Street's Friday rally — S&P 500 +0.73%, Dow +0.49%, Nasdaq +1.19% to a record high — came on the back of a weak September payrolls print (+29,000 vs. +84,000 expected) that cut October Fed-hike odds to roughly 17–21% from 64% a week earlier, even as the 10-year Treasury yield held at 5.28% and the 2-year at 4.83% following Chair Warsh's hawkish September hike to 3.75–4%. A bipartisan continuing resolution keeps Washington funded into early-to-mid December, removing shutdown risk through the midterm run-up. Brent and WTI firmed toward $102 and $91 respectively after China suspended oil-product exports, adding a fresh supply-tightening impulse on top of lingering Hormuz disruption. CNBC and NBC News.

legislative.policy_html: IMF Fourth EFF / Third RSF Review (from 23 Sep, Petrova-led mission) alongside a new requirement for 10,000 federal employees to digitally declare assets by 30 October.
legislative.impact_html: Wins: banks and the fiscal position if the roughly $1.2bn combined EFF/RSF tranche is unlocked; governance credibility from the asset-declaration drive. Loses: consumers if IMF-linked energy-tariff adjustments accompany the review; federal employees facing a tight compliance deadline.

legislative.policy_html: PIF 2026–2030 strategy reallocating roughly $41bn away from construction into digital infrastructure, alongside OPEC+'s decision to hold November output at 31.01m bpd.
legislative.sectors: Digital Infrastructure, Tourism, Construction, Energy, Shipping/Insurance
legislative.impact_html: Wins: PIF-backed digital-infrastructure and tourism assets; oil exporters benefiting from steady OPEC+ discipline and a firmer price. Loses: construction and contracting firms absorbing PIF's capex pivot; shippers and insurers still pricing a persistent Hormuz risk premium.

legislative.policy_html: Bipartisan continuing resolution funding the US government into early-to-mid December, alongside the Fed's hawkish September hike to 3.75–4% under Chair Warsh with a dot plot flagging one further 2026 move.
legislative.sectors: Federal Contractors, Rate-Sensitive Equities, Housing, Small-Caps
legislative.impact_html: Wins: federal agencies and contractors with funding certainty into the midterms; large-cap tech riding the Nasdaq's record run. Loses: rate-sensitive housing and small-cap names exposed if the Fed delivers its flagged additional 2026 hike.

levels.support_note: Monday's intraday low amid fresh selling; deeper support near 165,000
levels.resistance_note: Friday's intraday high; then 170,000 psychological resistance

desk_stance_html: The desk reads the tape as a continuation of the September–October risk-off drift rather than a one-off shock: three straight down sessions and a weak Monday open below 167,000 confirm that political noise and a renewed oil-price impulse are outweighing the modest support from firmer Oil & Gas Exploration names. Direction into the week hinges on three swing factors — the pace and tone of the IMF fourth EFF review, whether the China-driven oil supply tightening proves durable, and whether US yields ease further as October Fed-hold odds firm. We would treat a daily close back above 168,850 as the first sign of stabilisation, and a break below 166,550 as confirmation the slide extends toward 165,000. All levels are indicative desk estimates, not recommendations.

KSE-100 falls for a third straight session to 168,155 as political uncertainty meets a China-driven oil-price surge — even as Wall Street rallies to a Nasdaq record on cooling Fed-hike bets.

THE OVERNIGHT TAPE
US equities surged Friday after September payrolls rose just 29,000 versus 84,000 expected and unemployment ticked up to 4.2%: the S&P 500 gained 0.73% to 7,722.72, the Dow added 0.49% (+250.40 pts) to 51,176.96, and the Nasdaq jumped 1.19% to a record-high 27,190.86. CME FedWatch priced October Fed-hike odds at roughly 17-21%, down from 64% a week earlier, even as the 10-year Treasury yield closed at 5.28% and the 2-year at 4.83% following Chair Kevin Warsh's hawkish September debut hike to 3.75-4%. A bipartisan continuing resolution keeps Washington funded into early-to-mid December. Gold gave back its early jobs-data bounce to settle near $4,142.00 (-0.83%) and silver fell 1.04% to $60.23 as a firm dollar and elevated yields dominated. Brent settled at $102.25 and WTI at $91.11 after China suspended oil-product exports, tightening global fuel supply on top of lingering Strait of Hormuz disruption.

PAKISTAN
The KSE-100 fell for a third straight session, down 481.36 points (-0.29%) Friday to 168,155.49, after shedding 1,332.47 points (-0.78%) Thursday — a combined roughly 1,814-point slide. Total market volume slipped to 493.96 million shares on traded value of Rs17.49 billion, with decliners leading advancers 321 to 128 (45 unchanged) across 494 names; Commercial Banks dragged the index down 121.77 points while Oil & Gas Exploration Companies added 72.68 points. The index opened Monday under renewed pressure, falling over 1,600 points intraday to 166,554.66 as political uncertainty and the oil-price surge persisted. The SBP held its policy rate at 11.5% for a third straight meeting on 14 September as September CPI eased to 10.3% y/y (from August's 11.1%), and the rupee firmed 3 paisa to 277.07 interbank. An IMF mission under Iva Petrova continues the fourth EFF/third RSF review, kicked off by Finance Minister Aurangzeb on 29 September; a successful conclusion would unlock roughly $1.2 billion combined.

GCC
Saudi Arabia's non-oil PMI held at a six-month high of 57.8 in September as the Crown Prince's PIF 2026-2030 strategy reallocated roughly $41 billion from construction into Hormuz-immune digital infrastructure, with non-oil activity now 55% of non-oil GDP. OPEC+'s seven core producers held November output steady at 31.01 million bpd on 4 October, extending October's pause after four consecutive monthly hikes, with Gulf members still pumping only 60-80% of normal levels amid continuing Strait of Hormuz export disruption; the group next meets 1 November.

GLOBAL
A weak September jobs report reset Fed-hike expectations for October to roughly 17-21%, even as yields stayed elevated and Chair Warsh's dot plot continues to flag one further 2026 hike. Washington's bipartisan continuing resolution removes shutdown risk into the midterm run-up. China's suspension of oil-product exports added a fresh supply-tightening impulse to global crude markets.

LEGISLATIVE TRACKER
Pakistan: IMF fourth EFF/third RSF review + federal asset-declaration mandate — wins for banks and fiscal credibility if the $1.2bn tranche unlocks, risk for consumers facing energy-tariff adjustments.
GCC: PIF 2026-2030 capex pivot + OPEC+ November output hold — wins for digital-infrastructure and tourism plays, risk for construction firms and Hormuz-exposed shippers/insurers.
Global: US continuing resolution + Fed's hawkish hike-and-hold — wins for federally funded contractors and large-cap tech, risk for rate-sensitive housing and small-caps.

THE DAY AHEAD
KSE-100 support 166,550 (deeper support near 165,000) · pivot 168,155 · resistance 168,850 (then 170,000 psychological). Desk stance: a continuation of the September-October risk-off drift, not a one-off shock — treat a close back above 168,850 as the first stabilisation signal, and a break below 166,550 as confirmation the slide extends toward 165,000. All levels are indicative desk estimates, not recommendations.
